results.fact: Which slopes hold the hazardous snow
results.correct_value: the lingering steep snow lies on the slopes the trail itself crosses (southeast-facing switchbacks and the traverse to the pass/west side), not on north/east-facing slopes
results.evidence: The trail climbs southeast-facing slopes from Twin Lakes (which lie SE of the summit) and crests a pass to the western side at 1.3 mi (WTA); the snow hazard is the slope above the 0.9 mi junction that may be too dangerous to traverse (WTA), and the Forest Service describes steep, exposed snowfields on the trail lingering into August. Approach, waypoint directions, seasonal_hazards, partner requirements and the July note all place the snow on the south/southeast/west side the trail crosses; only hazards[0] said north/east. Rewrote that phrase neutrally rather than asserting an unsourced single aspect; "southeast slopes" vs "south/west traverse" describe consecutive parts of the same trail and were left.
